races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF 'Jersey Lily' Fillies' Nursery
races.verdict: A few potential improvers line up but at the foot of the weights, FIRE THUNDER makes lots of appeal having looked well suited by 7f last month, form boosted by the third since. Al Samsama, Sierra Belle and Polyxena all have something to recommend them.

runners.note: Blue Point filly who overcame inexperience to make a winning debut in a 6f Newbury maiden (firm) in July. Bare form of that nothing to get carried away with but she cemented a solid start to her career when runner-up und

Overcame obvious inexperience when a 40/1 winner on debut at Windsor in July (6f) and defied a penalty in the manner of a useful prospect over the same C&D 3 weeks later. 7f should be within range and she's in the right
Opened her account in Ayr maiden (7f, good to firm) prior to digging deep to make a successful nursery debut at Thirsk (good). Progress has levelled off since and she looks vulnerable to improvers.

Frankel filly who was a close second starting out the July Course (6f). Turned over at short odds in a small-field Salisbury novice next time but got it right switched to all-weather at Kempton 3 weeks ago. Limit not yet

Promising third on debut before finishing well held in the Sweet Solera. Got off the mark with sights lowered in a 1m novice (first 3 runs on the July Course) and this a far more suitable assignment than the Group 2 May
Awkward head carriage a feature of her early performances but she's found only one too good all 3 starts, upped to 7.5f at Beverley 10 days ago. Nursery debut.

Seen to maximum advantage when second of 7 on the July Course last month but surprisingly for one upped to 1m, she lacked a change of gear when last of 4 on all-weather debut. Nursery debut and yard hitting form.

Kingman filly who built on placed effort at Newbury on debut when landing short odds in 6f Ayr maiden last month. Didn't immediately reap the benefit of 7f on nursery debut at former track a week ago.
Promise amidst obvious inexperience first 2 starts and didn't need to improve to land the odds at Epsom on first try over 7f a month ago, driven out. Can remain competitive in handicaps.

Mehmas filly from a family her yard has had success with. Promising fourth starting out over 6f at Newbury in July and while she hasn't built on that twice since, she appeals as the type to progress with racing.

Sioux Nation filly who was runner-up on her first 3 starts before landing short odds in a weak race at Lingfield (6f) in July. Relished 7f when a fast-finishing second on the July Course last month and the third has adve

races.name: Market Square Monasterevin Irish European Breeders Fund Maiden
races.verdict: BENOWN made a promising start to his career when runner-up here last month, beaten only by a more streetwise rival, and he can build on that effort to go one better. Controlla is feared most dropped into a maiden for the first time, while Heralds March is one to note with his debut run behind him.

runners.note: Looks to have been brought along gradually in a trio of maidens so far, dropped back to 6f when sixth of 8 at Cork on latest outing. Will be of more appeal in handicaps.
Shaped with plenty of encouragement when second of 11 in maiden at this course (7f) on debut last month, nearest at the finish. Can make a bold bid with improvement to come.
Hinted at ability first time up when seventh of 11 in maiden at Naas (7f) 9 days ago, nearest at the finish having had to pick way through. This run should reveal more dropped in trip.
Attracted support and ran to a fair level on debut when seventh of 16 in maiden at this course (7f) 5 weeks ago. Clearly thought capable of better so he could be in the mix this time around.
Made an encouraging debut when second of 8 in maiden at Cork 17 days ago, travelling well for a long way behind an above-average prospect. Entitled to take a step forward from his first run.
Foaled March 27. 17,000 gns yearling, €13,000 2-y-o, Harry Angel gelding. Dam 1m/8.3f winner from a very good family. Has a useful standard to aim at on debut.
Foaled March 19. 175,000 gns foal, Blue Point colt. Dam unraced half-sister to useful 2-y-o 6f winner Nidhaal. Watch for market clues with yard also running Controlla.
Always behind in C&D maiden on debut and fared no better when well held at Naas 9 days ago. Looks to be up against it.

Big effort pitched into a Group 3 on debut when beaten only a neck by subsequent Queen Mary winner Victorious at Naas in May. Hasn't built on that effort since, though faced a stiff task in the Moyglare here (7f) 13 days

Foaled May 5. €10,000 yearling, Space Blues filly. Half-sister to several winners, including smart winner up to 7f Hamza (2-y-o 5f winner) and 7f-8.6f winner Grandstand. Dam maiden (stayed 1m) half-sister to very smart 5
Some encouragement on debut and stepped forward from that effort when 3¾ lengths eighth of 14 in maiden at Leopardstown (7f) 5 weeks ago. Will need to find more again in this contest.
Foaled March 21. Nando Parrado filly. Dam 6f winner. Faces a difficult task making her first start.
Foaled February 5. Ten Sovereigns filly. Dam unraced half-sister to smart winner up to 6f Encrypted out of useful French 1m winner Disclose. May just be better for this first experience.
Wasn't seen to best effect in valuable sales race at Naas on debut in August. Shaped as if amiss when eased off at Dundalk 6 weeks ago, but she's worth another chance to build on her initial promise.

races.name: William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap
races.verdict: Golden Mile runner-up CERULEAN BAY often goes well at this track and is taken to resume winning ways with his sights slightly lowered. Centigrade and Eternal Force are feared for the excellent Beckett and Haggas yards respectively, with both 4-y-os looking well treated on their best form.

runners.note: Top-end handicapper who hasn't fired on either start since a cracking second in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood. Does have a good record at this course, though, and looks well worth another chance with sights lowere

Free-going sort. On the up when successful at Newmarket/Epsom prior to having excuses in the Hunt Cup/Golden Mile. Shaped as though back in reasonable form when beaten 5 lengths at Doncaster (1m) last time and handicappe

Had some strong juvenile form prior to overcoming a 20-month absence in impressive style at Southwell in June. Never placed to justify favouritism in a well-contested York handicap before pulling away his chance in a lis

Only 2 lb higher than when landing the 2025 Lincoln for William Haggas, however, has been operating a notch below that level for a while now. Hasn't helped his cause by blowing the start on 2 of his 3 starts for present

Capped a productive 3-y-o season with a hat-trick success over C&D (good to soft) last October. Below par both starts since going close in a tactical race at Hamilton in June. Lurking on a dangerous mark if return to thi

Very much back on the up when completing a double over C&D (good to firm) last month. Seems unlikely to benefit from a strongly-run race on this occasion but still looked to be in good form when beaten 5¾ lengths in his

Ended useful juvenile season on a high when runner-up in 7f listed event at Chantilly. Wasn't beaten far despite trailing the field in the Craven on return. Gelded since finishing third in German Group 3 in April and see

Hasn't been seen to best effect on either start since finishing 4 lengths third in a solid York handicap in July. Given a chance by the handicapper following latest tardy start, though will need to be sharpened up by ret

Down the field in the Solario on the back of his Kempton novice win last summer. Much improved for return to front-running tactics when landing a useful handicap at Kempton latest. Mixed messages regarding the strength o

Never looked like justifying support when bidding to land a third career heavy-ground handicap at Goodwood in June. Tendency to race freely gives pause on return from 3 months away, and he could be one for later in the a

races.name: Theakston Brewing Legends Since 1827 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Having shaped encouragingly on his first 2 outings, BULLETSNAP wasn't able to find any progress at Windsor last time but he's well worth another chance for his leading yard. He gets the vote ahead of Scenic Route, who has offered plenty to work on in his 2 starts, while Time To Play could step forward from his debut run.

runners.note: Good-bodied colt but has finished well held both starts so far, albeit facing a very stiff task in valuable sales race at Doncaster (6.5f) 16 days ago. This run should reveal more.

Has made the frame in novices all 3 starts, showing promise at Goodwood and Doncaster on first 2 occasions (the winner from Doncaster now a useful type). Lesser effort when fourth of 9 at Windsor last month, but no surpr
Went with little promise on debut when seventh of 12 in novice at Redcar 5 weeks ago. Will need to leave that first effort well behind.
Didn't offer much first time up when finishing eighth of 9 in novice at Chester 15 days ago. Looks one for the longer term.
Down the field but hinted at ability when eleventh of 13 in maiden at Beverley (5f) on debut 10 days ago, making some progress after denied a clear run. Likely to need more time, though.

Foaled January 27. €62,000 yearling, Victor Ludorum colt. Half-brother to useful 6.5f/7f winner (including at 2 yrs) Half Sovereign. Has a fair standard to aim at making his first start. Wears tongue strap.

Runner-up to a subsequent Group 2 winner at Thirsk on debut and again shaped well when third of 11 in maiden at York (7f) 20 days ago, form which has been boosted since. Remains with potential and can make his presence f
€100,000 son of Blue Point who looked in need of the experience on debut when fourth of 7 in novice at Haydock 23 days ago. Could be in the mix with improvement to come from his first outing.
Has failed to beat a rival in his 2 outings, returning from 5 months off (gelded) when well held in 6-runner novice at Pontefract 9 days ago.

races.name: Tattersalls Online Royal Lodge Stakes (Group 2)
races.verdict: Perhaps best to narrow this down to unbeaten pair FIRST LAW and Burning Up. The former was snugly on top of Rocket Boy in a Haydock listed race 3 weeks ago and is narrowly preferred. The selection's stablemate Quest For Stars may prove best of the remainder.

runners.note: Too Darn Hot colt who is 2-2 in maiden/novice events over 1m at Haydock. Looks capable of making his presence felt in a higher grade.

1,000,000 gns Too Darn Hot colt who overcame inexperience on his 1m Sandown debut and saw off Rocket Boy in a listed race at Haydock (1m, soft) a month later. This smart prospect is the mount of William Buick from the Ch

Second in Group 2 Vintage at Goodwood before going one place better in the Acomb at York (7f, good). Well beaten in the Group 1 National Stakes at the Curragh since but he's a lot better than that. First attempt at 1m.

Made a promising winning start to his career in a 4-runner novice at Doncaster (7f, firm) in August. Bettered that form when second of 9 under a penalty at Leicester (7f, good) 18 days ago. Open to further progress but t

Won first 3 starts, notably a Salisbury listed event (1m, good). Lost his unbeaten record when 7 lengths third of 9 to Darkness Falls in 9f Group 1 at Leopardstown (good to firm) 14 days ago but it was another step forwa
500,000 gns Frankel colt who was undone by greenness on his 1m Newbury debut (good to firm) and made no mistake in another 1m maiden at Goodwood (heavy) 18 days ago. Sure to go on to better things.
Yarmouth debut winner. Placed behind reopposing pair Quest For Stars and First Law in 1m listed event since. The suspicion is he'll find at least one too strong again.

races.name: Kwiff More Bang For Your Bet Rated Race
races.verdict: A case can be made for most of these but INVINCIBLE WILL rates the pick at these weights and is fancied to bag a second C&D success at the chief expense of recent Leopardstown third Killashee Warrior. Lewis Carroll remains unexposed and can't be discounted after an absence, while Oro Blanco also needs factoring into this competitive event.

runners.note: Useful filly. Very good third of 18 in handicap at Leopardstown (1m, good to firm) 14 days ago. Must enter calculations.
C&D winner in May. 22/1, very good fifth of 14 in handicap at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) 13 days ago. Weighted to go close on these terms.
Debut winner in 6f Navan maiden last autumn. In decent form until coming in last of 6 in minor event at Fairyhouse (7f, good) in June. Needs to bounce back after a break.
Siyouni colt was much improved from his debut when landing 13-runner maiden over C&D (heavy) in March. Trainer going well so not ruled out despite his absence.
Landed 6f maiden on debut here last September. Lightly raced since but posted a solid fourth of 8 in minor event at Gowran (7f, soft) 7 days ago. This demands more though.
Progressive sort who got off the mark in 13-runner maiden at Navan (1m, good) 24 days ago, just holding on. Yard in good form so needs considering.
Opened his account in 7f Gowran handicap in August. Back on track with eleventh of 24 in handicap here (6f, good to soft) 13 days ago, not enjoying a clear run over 1f out. One to consider.
Bagged 7f Fairyhouse maiden and 6f Naas novice in June. Posted a good fourth of 17 in handicap at Leopardstown (7f, good to firm) 14 days ago. Trainer going well. Likely to continue in form.

Looked on the up when doubling his tally in 6f handicap at Listowel in May. Never able to land a blow off 7 lb higher when eighth of 14 in handicap here (6f, good to firm) following month. Not written off after a break.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap
races.verdict: ANCIENT STATE continues to progress and is fancied to bag a fifth victory of the season at the chief expense of multiple course scorer Trilby who acquitted himself really well in last week's Ayr Silver Cup and rates a big threat back here. Fandom is another who merits plenty of respect off a handy-looking mark, while last year's victor King of Light and in-form duo Hucklesbrook and Elara May also

runners.note: A 3-time winner in the US earlier in his career. Returned to his best when successful at Thirsk (6f) in May. Good third at Ascot (5f) in August and raced in unfavoured centre at Goodwood (6f, soft) last time. Weighted to
Impressed when a dual 5f scorer at Ffos Las and Ascot this summer. Not at his best in the mud when fourth of 6 in handicap at Goodwood (5f) 4 weeks ago, hanging badly right.

Took this 12 months ago and doubled his tally for present stable at Windsor (6f) in June. Back to form with fifth of 21 in Portland at Doncaster (5.5f, good) 2 weeks ago. Merits consideration once more eased 1 lb.

Continues on the up and more settled (usual eyeshields left off) when notching a fourth success of the season in 16-runner handicap at Doncaster (5f, good to firm) 13 days ago. Up 5 lb but this likeable sort merits serio

Rejuvenated by fitting of cheekpieces this season and notched a third success at Beverley (5f) in August. Posted another very good effort when sixth of 23 in Silver Cup at Ayr (6f, heavy) a week ago, coming home second i

Scored twice in 2025 for Oliver Cole, including in sales race at Newmarket (7f) in October. Hasn't managed to kick on this season, though, and well held both runs for his new yard at Ascot and Doncaster.

A useful 3-time 6f winner. Second run back from a breathing operation when a resurgent third of 12 to Rhythm N Hooves in handicap at Newbury (5f, good to firm) last month. Very much one to consider nudged up 1 lb.
Ended a losing sequence at Newbury (5f) in August but not best drawn when eighth of 12 in handicap at Ascot (5f, good to firm) 3 weeks ago. Not written off.

A fair 5f winner at 2 yrs who resumed with a very good second at York in May. Below that form since though, tried in a visor when eighth of 19 in handicap at York (5f, good) last month. This slow starter is not easy to m
A 4-time 5f winner at 2 yrs. Lightly raced this season but as good as ever when placed in handicaps at Yarmouth (5f) and over C&D recently. Well in the mix off the same mark.

Useful 5f winner at 2 yrs for Richard Fahey. Bounced back to form in first-time tongue tie to score over C&D in September but only sixteenth of 24 in Bronze Cup at Ayr (6f, soft) 8 days ago. More is required.
Won 5 times over the minimum trip in 2025. Hasn't fired so far this season, though, and this course scorer looks opposable unless market speaks firmly in his favour.

races.name: Lloyd Landrover Ripon Nursery (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: ZARAKOVA is a lightly-raced filly on the up and rates the one to beat, having improved again despite meeting trouble on nursery debut last time. Forest Berry has won twice recently and remains on an upward curve, so rates the chief threat, while Aphra Behn is also respected.

runners.note: 190,000 gns Zarak filly who made the most of her experience when getting off the mark in 4-runner maiden at Newmarket (1m) in August. Improved again despite meeting trouble when 2½ lengths fifth of 6 to Primal in nursery

Improved to win at Wolverhampton and then Musselburgh in August, and bettered the form of both of those successes when ¾-length fourth of 8 to Magnesium in nursery at Kempton last time despite making her effort earlier t
Improved when ¾-length second of 9 to Magic Harry in novice at Leicester last time. Will be suited by the step up to 1m on nursery debut but will need to find some improvement to come out on top.

Opened her account at the third time of asking in 7f Doncaster maiden in June, making the most of her experience. Hasn't kicked on in nurseries since, though, having no excuses when fourth of 5 to Kodi Bear Light at Newm
Son of Starspangledbanner who has yet to match the form of May's promising debut fourth at York (6f) in 3 subsequent outings, including on nursery debut on latest.

Has reached the frame on all 4 starts, matching previous form when 2¾ lengths third of 9 to Silver Sovereign in novice at Haydock. Will be suited by the step up to 1m and her opening mark is a fair one. Respected.

races.name: Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes (Fillies' Group 1)
races.verdict: A much-anticipated renewal, with preference for SUN GODDESS who again made an excellent impression when powering clear for victory in the Moyglare at the Curragh, taking her record to 5 from 7. She can provide her leading yard with a third consecutive win in this Group 1, though Senorita Bonita and Libertango have also looked exciting fillies and are much respected.

runners.note: Made a winning debut with something to spare at Fairyhouse and, quickly up in grade, showed much improved form when third behind 2 of today's rivals in Group 2 at the July Festival at this venue. Comfortable winner of 7f

Made it 2 from 2 when landing the Albany at Royal Ascot, with Sun Goddess in second. Not quite in the same form when runner-up to Senorita Bonita in Group 2 at the July Festival, but got back on the up with a strong-trav

Has gone the right way with each of her 4 starts, following her runner-up effort in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot with Group 3 success at the same course a month later. Overcame her wide draw when making all in Siren

Looked a very good prospect when making a winning debut at Nottingham and has progressed with each run since, getting the better of Libertango in Group 2 at the July Festival at this venue. Stormed clear for success in t

Runner-up twice in maidens from her first 4 starts, before taking a step forward when third in listed race at Leopardstown (7f) 2 weeks ago. However, she looks to face a tough ask upped further in grade, whilst she could

Continues to go from strength to strength, recording a first success at the highest level in the Phoenix at the Curragh, before overcoming significant interference in sales race at York. Added another Group 1 with an imp

races.name: Market Rasen Racecourse Conference & Events Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Southwell bumper winner NO MORE TEARDROPS may prolong Elated's wait for a breakthrough success. Harry Derham's newcomer Poets Pearl looks a likely danger, especially if supported.

runners.note: Might have overhauled the eventual winner bar a late fall at Worcester (2m) last month. Couldn't peg back a 150/1 shot who'd stolen a few mid-race lengths when runner-up over the same C&D subsequently. Sets the standard,
Flat-bred mare who showed only greenness on debut at Newton Abbot 8 days ago.
Modest 7f/1m handicapper on the Flat. Hardly looks an obvious type first time up over hurdles.
Well held in pair of bumpers 4 months apart. Showed a bit more when beaten 11½ lengths on hurdling debut at Worcester (2m, 200/1). Probably needs more time.
Stable second string when well beaten on debut at Sedgefield (17f, 40/1). Turned out relatively quickly by her excellent yard and the market should offer plenty of clues.

Mastercraftsman filly. Dam Grade 1 winning hurdler at Cheltenham Festival. Travelled well/knuckled down to make a winning start for the Twiston-Davies stable in a handy Southwell mares bumper in April. Now sent hurdling

€16,000 3-y-o, £30,000 4-y-o, Poet's Word filly. Dam, unraced, closely related to smart hurdler/high-class chaser (stayed 4m) Ballyoptic and fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser (stayed 3¾m) Sharp Response. Fourth in an I
Long-standing maiden on the Flat. Well beaten both hurdle starts at Sedgefield.
Dam half-sister to fairly useful hurdler (17f winner) Arslan. Modest form on Flat (stays 8.5f) for Ralph Beckett. Looks a handicap project on the evidence of her 2 starts to date.

races.name: Kwiff Supercharged Joe McGrath Handicap (Premier Handicap)
races.verdict: KEKE won this corresponding event in 2024 and he gets the vote with Colin Keane taking over. Stable-switcher Bounty completes a strong hand for the Edward Lynam yard, with Namiid and Stag Night other likely players in a wide-open renewal.

runners.note: C&D winner who was successful in listed company earlier in the season. Well treated on his close third in Premier Handicap at Cork in July and cheekpieces go back on following an effort that was too bad to be true there
Several good efforts in defeat this year. Latest 5¼-length defeat by Moltophino wasn't one of them and he's weighted to extend his long losing run here.

Won this corresponding event in 2024. Notched an eighth career success at Naas in July. Shaped better than the beaten distance here (6f) last time. Cheekpieces go on and makes plenty of appeal in a race that'll be run to
Isn't the easiest to win with. Best not judged too harshly on his latest run here (6f), travelling well but getting pretty much no luck whatsoever. Big-field 5f handicap could suit his style, though.

Won a trio of sprint handicaps at this venue last season. Improved form when runner-up to subsequent Group-1 winner in 5f listed race at Naas in May. Hasn't reproduced that effort, though, and work to do at the weights b
Forward-going type who posted a career best when scoring over C&D in August. Below form in a hot 6f sprint here last time. Weighted to be competitive if back on song returned to minimum trip.
Won Convivial maiden at York (7f) last summer for Aidan O'Brien. Has rather lost his way for current yard and leap of faith required dropped to 5f for handicap bow.

Back to very best when narrow winner over C&D in April (heavy). Not in the same form under contrasting conditions here in late-June. Still on a handy mark for in-form yard, for all he ideally needs more rain.

Useful sprinter. Looked up to defying this sort of mark when close fourth at Naas (5f, soft) on final start for Aidan O'Brien in October. Changed hands for 50,000 gns and capable new yard add a tongue strap for his retur

Fine third over C&D in early-summer. Back on the up when winning 12-runner handicap at Dundalk and still in good form when 3½ lengths sixth (not ideally placed) here (6f) last time. Solid chance at the weights, though dr

Useful sprinter who proved better than ever in first-time tongue strap when taking 11-runner handicap at Naas last month. Only beaten by an improved British raider in a big-field course handicap (6f) since. No surprise i
Built on his C&D second when landing a 5f Naas handicap last time, quickening to score by ¾ length from Namiid. Seems revitalised by blinkers and cannot be discounted in his current vein of form.
In-form sprinter who was clear of the remainder when ¾-length second of 8 to Moltophino at Navan last time. Reopposes on better terms here and could run a big race for yard firmly among the winners.

Free-going sort who made a winning return in maiden at Cork (5f) in April. Tongue strap on for first time when beaten 5 lengths in listed race there last time. Big-field event may suit better, however, the handicapper ha

Low-mileage sprinter. Showed improved form when opening account with a ready success in 12-runner handicap at Cork. Ran a cracker off her revised mark when ¾-length second at Navan since (form taken a few knocks). Still

C&D winner who made the frame twice here this summer. Reported to have lost a shoe when finding run of good form coming to a halt at Navan latest. Course record suggests he's an each-way player from 3 lb out of handicap.

Son of Starman who knew what was required to make a winning start at Yarmouth last October. Turned over at short odds on final start for Michael Bell in June (sold for only 2,500 gns) and probably up against it on handic
One-time useful sprinter for Marco Botti. Hasn't gone on from his 6f win here in June. Races from 3 lb out of the handicap with usual headgear back on.
Won at Dundalk on final 2 starts last year and also scored at the same course in March. Step back in right direction when fourth at Navan last time. This a stronger race than he need contest, though.
Built on promise of previous couple of efforts when winning comfortably over C&D last month. Remains well treated on old form, though this is a much deeper race (long way out the weights).

races.name: British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Roger Varian continues among the winners and his KAGUYAHIME is fancied to add to the tally on the back of a promising initial third at Ascot, form which gives her the clear edge here. Karl Burke's She's Got A Way rates the chief threat if, as expected, taking a sizeable step forward from her debut Doncaster third over this longer trip. My Girl Dee Mo and Woollahra can fight it out for minor honour

runners.note: Foaled February 23. €55,000 foal, 145,000 gns yearling, Palace Pier filly. Half-sister to 3 winners, including useful 2-y-o 5f winner Magical Journey and useful 7f-9.5f winner Sceptic. Very much one to consider on her de

Sent off 11/1 but made a promising start when third of 10 in maiden at Ascot (1m, good) 22 days ago, taking third late on under hand riding. This Starspangledbanner filly is open to a fair bit of progress and looks the o

Sent off 18/1 and hooded for her debut but shaped encouragingly with fifth of 9 in novice at Salisbury (1m, good to soft) 23 days ago. Blinkers go on now and this daughter of Camelot is open to improvement.
Unable to justify 7/4 favouritism but shaped well when an initial third of 4 in novice over C&D (heavy) 22 days ago. This Almanzor filly is capable of better.
Minzaal filly shaped well when a debut third of 7 in novice here (7f, good to soft) 23 days ago. Should improve but needs to on that bare form.
Foaled April 2. Nathaniel filly. Dam, 1m winner, half-sister to smart 1¼m-1½m winner abroad Mutamakina (by Nathaniel). The market can prove a good guide for this newcomer.

Lope De Vega filly fetched 750,000 gns as a yearling. Raced green when a promising third of 4 in maiden at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) on debut 15 days ago, taking third late on. Looks open to fair bit of progress, espe
110,000 gns Sea The Stars filly. Shaped as if needing the run when fourth of 7 on debut at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) in August. Rates a likely improver with step up in trip promising to suit.
Showcasing filly took a step forward from her debut with fourth of 8 in novice at Leicester (7f, good) 18 days ago. Can progress again stepped up to 1m.

races.name: John Lynch Memorial Maiden Hurdle
races.verdict: TRUBSHAW is a 3-time Flat winner and looks to have been found a winnable opportunity on hurdles debut. Je Suis Celebre seemed set to place on hurdling debut before falling and rates the chief threat, with that form since boosted by Golden Handshake and Approval. Lightly-raced Blue Johnl improved last time and is also respected.

runners.note: Maiden pointer who is bred to stay well but stepped up on previous hurdling efforts when 14 lengths second of 11 to First Ascent in 2m maiden at Kilbeggan 23 days ago.
Blue Bresil gelding who did no more than hint at ability when mid-division in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan on debut and is probably one for handicaps later on.
Offered little in 3 starts on the level for current yard this summer and has fared no better in 2 outings over hurdles.
€1,600 3-y-o, third foal, dam unraced half-sister to smart hurdler/high-class chaser (2m-23f winner) Hidden Cyclone. Yard are not known for winning debutants.

Showed ability on the Flat and looked set to place on debut for this yard when falling 3 out in maiden hurdle at Killarney last month, only a length down in second at the time. That form has since been boosted by the win

Fifth foal: dam (h116), 2¼m-21f hurdle winner (stayed 3m), also 17f-21.6f winner on Flat, half-sister to temperamental bumper winner/fair hurdler (stayed 2¼m) Rathmuck Native. Yard can ready a newcomer, so worth a market

Shirocco gelding who was runner-up on sole start in points and offered something to work on sent hurdling when 29½ lengths eighth of 16 to Minella Hollow in maiden at Killarney last month. Handicaps over longer trips are

Fifth foal, half-brother to fair hurdler/chase winner Nettuno Italia (2¾m-23f winner, by Imperial Monarch). Dam, point winner/ran twice over hurdles, half-sister to fairly useful 3m hurdle winner Kit Casey.
Bred to stay well and merely looks to be marking his time in maidens until tackling handicaps over 2½m+.

Fairly useful performer at up to 2¼m on the Flat. Won a handicap at Killarney in August and shaped as if still in good form at Down Royal earlier this month. Goes without usual headgear now switched to hurdling but in ve
Well held in a bumper and in 2 maiden hurdles.

Opened his account in 6f Hamilton novice in May. Back on track in first-time cheekpieces when a staying-on third of 13 on nursery bow at Ayr (6f, soft) 8 days ago. Ought to be thereabouts with this longer trip a likely p

Debut 6f novice winner here in May. Runner-up twice since but came in last of 11 in first-time cheekpieces in nursery at Chester (7f, heavy) a week ago. Has it to prove now.

races.name: Michael Raby Memorial Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: SHOWTIME MAHOMES took a step in the right direction when third last time and races from the same career-low mark here so he's taken to resume winning ways. Big Apple Jack finally broke his duck last time and should go well from just a 3 lb higher mark, while Good Karma is so consistent that he's hard to see being out of the frame.

Won over C&D in May but lost his way since leaving Ben Haslam, running poorly in a change of headgear last time. Hard to fancy on recent evidence.
Continues to hold his form, only outside the frame once across his last 10 outings. Creditable third of 12 in a handicap at Pontefract 9 days ago and likely to go well once more.

Finally got off the mark in a 13-runner handicap at Hamilton 24 days ago, first-time blinkers perhaps adding an edge. Up 3 lb but likely still feasibly treated so could follow up now he's got the hang of things.

Dropped to a mark in the 50s for the first time when third of 11 in a handicap at Catterick over 7f 18 days ago, faring best of those ridden with the pace. Back down in trip to 6f and one to note at this level.
Maiden improving gradually with each run, finishing second of 6 at Catterick 18 days ago on his third start. Needs bigger step forward up against older horses on handicap debut.
Twice a winner over C&D in 2024 and ended losing run when scoring twice from lowly marks this May. Largely consistent since but needs to settle better than she did last time.
Twice a winner at Chelmsford earlier this year but first finish outside the frame in 2026 coincided with recent return to turf so she's got surface concerns.

races.name: Michael Raby Memorial Handicap
Gent's Night Sat 24th October Handicap
races.verdict: LET'S GO HUGO has been rejuvenated since being refitted with cheekpieces and can notch a fourth win in just over a month. Mimime arrives in good form and can pose the biggest threat ahead of Protest Rally.

runners.note: Dual winner in May 2025 prior to edging down the weights and offered something to work on returning from a year off when fifth of 9 in handicap (66/1) at Catterick (5f, good) 18 days ago, not knocked about. Cheekpieces b

Won 4 times on all-weather in second half of 2025. Also started 2026 with some creditable efforts but hasn't shown enough back on turf in recent months to be too positive here.
4-time C&D winner, the latest from a 6 lb higher mark in January. More miss than hit since though and was down the field here when last seen back in May.

Has been given a chance by the handicapper and wasn't disgraced when fourth of 8 over C&D in June. Down the field upped to 6f when last seen here 41 days ago, though, and has a bit to prove on balance.
Placed twice at C&D on his last 2 outings in 2024 but little encouragement in 2 recent starts since returning from a near 2-year absence.

Got off the mark for Ollie Sangster at Wolverhampton (6f) in July. Not in same form under a penalty at Chepstow next time and might've needed the run making his debut for this yard at Leicester 18 days ago.
Hasn't kicked on from promising second start for current yard on all-weather in May, failing to beat a rival in a 9-runner event at Windsor last month. Lots to prove at present.

Lightly-raced filly is improving steadily and produced her best effort to date when bumping into a well-treated rival for the second start in a row over C&D 9 days ago. Leading player despite being 1 lb out of the weight

races.name: Blandford Bloodstock 25th Anniversary EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: The market should prove highly revealing but the vote goes to RUBY SANDS who shaped well on her debut when third at Newbury and can build on it to get off the mark with Tom Marquand aboard. Roger Varian continues among the winners and his newcomers Miss Jane Hadley (second choice) and Out Late both make plenty of appeal. Queen Of The Gulf and Aquila D'Oro are other debutantes who also command resp

runners.note: Foaled April 18. 170,000 gns yearling, Gleneagles filly. Closely related to useful 7f winner Poetry of Time and half-sister to 2-y-o 7f winner Biniorella Bay. The market should give a good guide to this newcomer.
14/1, slowly away when tenth of 12 in novice at Kempton (7f) on debut 45 days ago. This Mehmas filly needs to take a big step forward.

Sent off 10/1 when last of 4 in maiden at Ascot (6f, good to firm) on debut 3 weeks ago. Much more is required from this daughter of Showcasing.
Foaled March 4. Blackbeard filly. Half-sister to useful 7f winner Miss Carol Ann and US 1m winner Instability. Noteworthy newcomer from in-form yard. Well worth a market check.
Foaled April 15. €180,000 yearling, Blue Point filly. Half-sister to 7f winner Norfolk Blue. Makes plenty of appeal on paper and stable among the winners.
Made a promising start with second of 6 in novice at Lingfield (1m, all-weather) last month, taking second late on. This Time Test filly seems sure to build on it.

Well-related Sands of Mali filly who made a promising start with third of 7 in novice at Newbury (6.5f, good to firm) in July. Capable of better and holds very good claims with Ryan Moore in the saddle.
Foaled April 27. 320,000 gns yearling, Sea The Stars filly. Half-sister to 2-y-o 7f winner Senor Campanaro. Dam British/German winner up to 1m (including at 2 yrs). A considered debutant.

races.name: Goffs Million
races.verdict: A range of abilities on show with TREAN given the tentative vote down in class having shaped as though still in top form in the Group 1 National Stakes over C&D 2 weeks ago. Carry The Flag is a huge threat on form but with 7f not certain to suit, Green Dreamer could be the chief threat.

€70,000 yearling, Starspangledbanner filly who knew more than on debut when fourth of 5 at Cork 17 days ago but this is asking a lot at this stage of her career.

races.name: Dine In Altior's Restaurant Handicap Chase

Veteran Ribeye also has a more favourable weight pull with Huckleberry Sting and is second choice.

races.name: Kathleen Walsh Memorial Handicap Hurdle (0-100)
races.verdict: LALIGURASH proved a different proposition when only narrowly denied at Killarney last time and, with better still to come upped further in trip, he could be ready to get off the mark. Tropical Image was successful at this meeting a year ago and heads the list of dangers, with Annie Button and Opposite Ends also in the mix.

Making her third start in maiden hurdles, showed a bit more than previously when fifth of 11 at Kilbeggan (19f) 23 days ago. Remains capable of better as she goes up in trip for handicap debut.

Not much encouragement in bumpers/maiden hurdles for Patrick T. Foley and hasn't fared any better in 2 handicaps for current yard, stopping quickly at Tramore (2½m) 6 weeks ago.

races.name: J&P Civil Engineering British EBF Maiden Stakes
races.verdict: A few of these bring potential but the vote goes to IMPASTO who shaped very well when a debut runner-up in a strong Ascot maiden (form working out well) and can go one better now. Both Hands To Yourself and Royal Acclamation also look to have better days ahead of them and can also have a say.

races.name: Michael Raby Memorial Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: HURSTWOOD won twice at Redcar before completing a hat-trick over C&D in September 2022 and is taken to repeat the feat 4 years on. Kings Merchant has his 2 lb rise for his recent Catterick success more than offset by the promising Conor Whiteley's claim and is second choice ahead of Valentine Catcher and Angel Summer.

races.verdict: ROMOTOSO showed form akin to that of her debut when finding only one too good in a Windsor novice 3 weeks ago and a repeat may well be enough to see William Knight's filly get off the mark. Inglewood and Shaniko are 2 live threats, though, with Mollisha also needing to be factored in having had a plausible excuse at Chester last time.

races.name: Book The Bistro In Seasons Restaurant Apprentice Handicap
races.verdict: IZZARI and Ballybunion both shaped much better than the bare result last time with the former shading the vote. Gladiadora made it 2 from 2 here in good style recently so she's another to consider.

races.verdict: MASSIMO BLUE made a fine start for this yard when winning twice over C&D last month and he can regain the winning thread after a rare slow break put him on the back foot last time. The reliable Come On Over is also shortlisted alongside Mr Cool, who should benefit from the step back up to 6f.
